title: Curry with a fever
setting: Saturday morning. Kenta phones Yuki to fix a time for the movie they planned, but she is in bed feeling awful.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, yuki? kyou no eiga, nanji ni suru?
lines.ja: もしもし、ユキ？今日の映画、何時にする？
lines.kana: もしもし、ゆき？きょうのえいが、なんじにする？
lines.english: Hey, Yuki? What time do you want to do the movie today?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, kenta. gomen, kyou, nanka darukute.
lines.ja: あ、ケンタ。ごめん、今日、なんかだるくて。
lines.kana: あ、けんた。ごめん、きょう、なんかだるくて。
lines.english: Oh, Kenta. Sorry, today I'm kind of... not feeling it.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: darui? e, eiga iku no ga darui no? hidoi naa.
lines.ja: だるい？え、映画行くのがだるいの？ひどいなあ。
lines.kana: だるい？え、えいがいくのがだるいの？ひどいなあ。
lines.english: Not feeling it? What, you can't be bothered to go to the movie? Harsh.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sou ja nakute, karada ga darui no! kinou no yoru, netsu deta n da.
lines.ja: そうじゃなくて、体がだるいの！昨日の夜、熱出たんだ。
lines.kana: そうじゃなくて、からだがだるいの！きのうのよる、ねつでたんだ。
lines.english: Not like that! I mean my body feels all heavy. I came down with a fever last night.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.kana: え、ねつでたの？だいじょうぶ？
lines.english: Wait, you got a fever? Are you okay?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: uun, mada sanjuuhachido mo netsu aru.
lines.ja: ううん、まだ38度も熱ある。
lines.kana: ううん、まださんじゅうはちどもねつある。
lines.english: Not really. I've still got a fever of 38.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: uwa, takai ne. seki toka wa?
lines.kana: うわ、たかいね。せきとかは？
lines.english: Yikes, that's high. Any cough or anything?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: seki mo deru shi, hanamizu mo deru shi, mou saiaku.
lines.ja: 咳も出るし、鼻水も出るし、もう最悪。
lines.kana: せきもでるし、はなみずもでるし、もうさいあく。
lines.english: I've got a cough, my nose is running... it's the worst.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.ja: そっか、風邪ひいちゃったんだ。
lines.kana: そっか、かぜひいちゃったんだ。
lines.english: Ah, so you've caught a cold.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un. a, kenta mo kinou, seki deteta yo ne?
lines.ja: うん。あ、ケンタも昨日、咳出てたよね？
lines.kana: うん。あ、けんたもきのう、せきでてたよね？
lines.english: Yeah. Oh, wait. You had a cough yesterday too, didn't you?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e? a, un. hanamizu mo deteta. netsu wa denakatta kedo.
lines.ja: え？あ、うん。鼻水も出てた。熱は出なかったけど。
lines.kana: え？あ、うん。はなみずもでてた。ねつはでなかったけど。
lines.english: Huh? Oh, yeah. And a runny nose. I didn't get a fever, though.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sore da! kenta no kaze ga utsutta n da!
lines.ja: それだ！ケンタの風邪がうつったんだ！
lines.kana: それだ！けんたのかぜがうつったんだ！
lines.english: That's it! I caught your cold!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: gomen! eiga wa raishuu ikou. nanka tsukutte motte iku yo.
lines.ja: ごめん！映画は来週行こう。なんか作って持っていくよ。
lines.kana: ごめん！えいがはらいしゅういこう。なんかつくってもっていくよ。
lines.english: Sorry! Let's do the movie next week. I'll cook something and bring it over.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: honto? jaa, kenta no karee ga ii.
lines.ja: ほんと？じゃあ、ケンタのカレーがいい。
lines.kana: ほんと？じゃあ、けんたのカレーがいい。
lines.english: Really? Then I want your curry.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.english: Curry? When you've got a fever?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un. karada wa darui kedo, karee nara taberareru.
lines.ja: うん。体はだるいけど、カレーなら食べられる。
lines.kana: うん。からだはだるいけど、カレーならたべられる。
lines.english: Yep. My body feels like lead, but curry I can always manage.

questions.english: What happens in this phone call?

choices.english: Yuki can't be bothered to go to the movie today, so Kenta gets annoyed and goes without her.
Kenta has caught Yuki's cold, so she offers to cook curry and bring it to him.
Yuki is sick, probably with Kenta's cold, so the movie moves to next week and Kenta will bring her food.

questions.explanation: Lines 2-4: Yuki's 'nanka darukute' is not about the movie, as Kenta guesses in line 3; she means karada ga darui, and a fever came on last night (netsu deta). Lines 6-8: she still has a fever of 38, a cough and a runny nose. Lines 10-12: Kenta had a cough and a runny nose yesterday, so she decides she caught his cold (kenta no kaze ga utsutta). Line 13: the movie moves to next week (eiga wa raishuu ikou) and Kenta will cook something and bring it over; line 14: she asks for his curry. A is Kenta's misreading, which Yuki corrects in line 4 (sou ja nakute), and nobody goes without her. B swaps the two: it is Yuki who caught Kenta's cold (line 12), and Kenta is the one cooking (lines 13-14: kenta no karee).

questions.english: Now you're the one in bed with the cold. Kenta drops by with curry and asks, "netsu wa dou?" (How's the fever?) It hasn't gone down. Tell him you still have a fever.
questions.answer: Say the fever is still there, with netsu and aru: un, mada netsu aru yo.

modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I've still got a fever.

modelAnswers.ja: まだちょっと熱ある。37度。
modelAnswers.english: Still a bit of a fever. 37.

questions.explanation: A fever you have right now is netsu ga aru: the fever 'exists'. That is Yuki's 'mada sanjuuhachido mo netsu aru' in line 6 and Kenta's 'netsu aru noni?' in line 15. English 'have' pulls toward motsu, but you never netsu o motsu. And netsu deta (line 4) is the moment it came on, not the fever you still have; in casual speech ga drops: netsu aru.

questions.english: When Yuki tells Kenta what happened last night, what does she say?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、昨日の夜のことを何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、きのうのよるのことをなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, kinou no yoru no koto o nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Last night I turned into a fever.
choices.romaji: kinou no yoru, netsu ni natta n da.

choices.english: I came down with a fever last night.
choices.romaji: kinou no yoru, netsu deta n da.

choices.english: Last night I received a fever.
choices.romaji: kinou no yoru, netsu moratta n da.

questions.explanation: Line 4: kinou no yoru, netsu deta n da, and Kenta echoes it in line 5 (e, netsu deta no?). A fever 'comes out': netsu ga deru, with the past deta for the moment it came on. A, netsu ni naru, is English 'get' read as 'become'; Japanese doesn't say it. C, morau, is 'get' word for word; with illness it is only for catching a cold from someone (kenta no kaze moratta), never for a fever itself. For the cold she caught from Kenta, Yuki uses kaze ga utsuru (line 12).

questions.english: A few days later you've caught it too. Yuki phones, hears you coughing, and asks, "kaze hiita no? netsu aru?" (Did you catch a cold? Got a fever?) You have no fever, but you do have a cough. Tell her.
questions.kana: かぜひいたの？ねつある？
questions.answer: Say no fever, but a cough with seki and deru: netsu wa nai kedo, seki ga deru n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, netsu wa nai kedo, seki ga deru n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、熱はないけど、咳が出るんだ。
modelAnswers.english: No, no fever, but I've got a cough.

modelAnswers.romaji: netsu wa nai. demo, seki ga sugoku deru.
modelAnswers.ja: 熱はない。でも、咳がすごく出る。
modelAnswers.english: No fever. But I'm coughing a lot.

questions.explanation: A cough 'comes out' like a fever does: seki ga deru, the same deru as Yuki's 'seki mo deru shi' in line 8 and her 'seki deteta yo ne?' to Kenta in line 10. English 'have a cough' pulls toward aru or motsu, but a cough that keeps coming takes deru. For coughing at this very moment, seki shiteru also works. Netsu wa nai is the negative of netsu ga aru.

questions.english: Next week at the movie, Yuki is still getting over her cold. She catches you staring and asks, "nani? nani miteru no?" (What? What are you looking at?) Her nose is running. Tell her.
questions.answer: Tell her her nose is running, with hanamizu and deru in the -teru form: hanamizu deteru yo.

modelAnswers.ja: ユキ、鼻水出てる。大丈夫？
modelAnswers.english: Yuki, your nose is running. You okay?

questions.explanation: A runny nose is hanamizu ga deru, 'nose water comes out'; English 'runny' has nothing to copy. Deteru is 'is coming out right now', as Kenta's 'hanamizu mo deteta' in line 11 is 'was running'. Yuki uses the plain form for her symptoms in line 8 (hanamizu mo deru shi). Between friends ga drops: hanamizu deteru yo.

questions.english: Kenta first thinks Yuki doesn't feel like going out. Then she says "sou ja nakute, karada ga darui no!" What does she mean?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、今どうですか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、いまどうですか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, ima dou desu ka?

choices.english: Her body feels heavy and run-down, the way it does when you're getting sick.
Going out today feels like too much of a drag.
She's worn out from doing too much yesterday.

questions.explanation: Line 4: karada ga darui is the heavy, sluggish feeling with no clear cause, and she adds straight away that a fever came on last night. She says it again in line 16 (karada wa darui kedo, karee nara taberareru). B is Kenta's misreading in line 3: darui on its own about something you have to do (eiga iku no ga darui) is a casual 'what a drag', which is why Yuki says sou ja nakute. C would be tsukareta, tired from effort; Yuki mentions no effort, only the fever, the cough and the runny nose.

newWords.english: kind of, sort of (filler); something (nanka tsukutte = make something)
